short: A long-range American fighter that provided critical escort for Allied bombers over Germany.
full:
The North American P-51 Mustang was originally designed in 1940 to a British purchasing commission specification for a new fighter. Initially hampered by limited high-altitude performance, the aircraft was transformed when its American Allison engine was replaced by a license-built Rolls-Royce Merlin. The resulting P-51B and P-51D variants possessed exceptional range, allowing them to escort Allied heavy bombers from bases in Britain all the way to targets deep within Germany and back.

The introduction of the Mustang in large numbers broke the back of the Luftwaffe's fighter arm, significantly reducing bomber losses and securing air superiority over Europe prior to the D-Day landings. It was similarly effective in the Pacific theatre, escorting B-29s over Japan. The Mustang remained in service during the Korean War as a ground-attack aircraft and was operated by various international air forces for decades.
